newsitem.title: JAPAN: MORNING SPORT-PROSPECTS UNCLEAR FOR VILLENEUVE, HILL.
newsitem.headline: MORNING SPORT-PROSPECTS UNCLEAR FOR VILLENEUVE, HILL.

text.p: World title contenders Damon Hill of Britain and Jacques Villeneuve of Canada were overshadowed by the wet weather and form of their rivals in Friday's opening practice for Sunday's Japanese Grand Prix.

The two Williams drivers, who will be racing for the world drivers' championship in the final round of the season, wound up fifth and fourth respectively -- a full second off the pace of fastest man Gerhard Berger.

Austrian Berger, in a Benetton, clocked the best time of one minute and 42.350 seconds at an average speed of 206.257 kph around the figure-of-eight Suzuka track. Second quickest was Mika Hakkinen of Finland in a McLaren ahead of double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany in his Ferrari.

Neither Villeneuve nor Hill suggested their performances bore any relation to the likely outcome of Saturday's qualifying session and both said they were satisfied with their day's work in preparation for the contest which lies ahead.

"It was useful on two counts," said Hill. "We were able to get some very useful wet weather running in and we also had a chance to do some dry running. So, we got a lot of information today, which will be very useful."
"It wasn't a waste of time," Villeneuve said after practising in the wet weather. "There is always a chance that the race may take place in these sort of conditions."
Hill leads Villeneuve by nine points in the title race and requires only one point from Sunday's 53 lap-race to clinch his first championship, even if Villeneuve wins.
This result would leave them level on 88 points but Hill would win because he has won seven races already this season to Villeneuve's four.
If Villeneuve fails to win, Hill will be champion wherever he finishes in the race.
Both men have pledged to an honourable contest with no deliberate collisions of the sort which have marred the event in the past.
